title: Injective model structures for ordinary small diagrams
statement: Use the model-category conventions of [lem-coef-reedy-model-structure]: a complete and cocomplete category $\mathcal M$ with functorial weak factorization systems $(\mathrm{Cof},\mathrm{Fib}\cap W)$ and $(\mathrm{Cof}\cap W,\mathrm{Fib})$, with $W$ retract closed and satisfying two-out-of-three. Suppose $\mathcal M$ is combinatorial: it is locally presentable, meaning generated under $\kappa$-filtered colimits by a small set of objects whose Hom functors preserve those colimits for some regular cardinal $\kappa$, and both weak factorization systems are generated by sets. Let $A$ be any small ordinary category. The ordinary functor category $\operatorname{Fun}(A,\mathcal M)$ has a functorial combinatorial injective model structure: weak equivalences and cofibrations are objectwise, and fibrations are the maps having the right lifting property against every objectwise trivial cofibration. Every injective fibration is objectwise a fibration. The constant diagram functor $\Delta:\mathcal M\to\operatorname{Fun}(A,\mathcal M)$ is left Quillen, with right adjoint the strict limit. Consequently, for an injectively fibrant replacement $H\xrightarrow{\sim}RH$, a cone $C\to\lim_A H$ is homotopy limiting precisely when its comparison $C\to\lim_A RH$ is a weak equivalence; the condition is independent of the choice of replacement. No simplicial enrichment of $\mathcal M$ is assumed. The case $A=\varnothing$ is included. Universes are enlarged to contain the small diagram and the categories of diagrams.

source.place: Proposition A.2.8.2, Remark A.2.8.5, Proposition A.2.8.7(2) and definition of homotopy right Kan extension following it, printed pp.830-833. Read online 2026-10-17; archival HTT WANTED. No Stacks tag states this homotopical theorem.

proof.text: Use the model conventions in [lem-coef-reedy-model-structure]. Equip the underlying ordinary category $\mathcal M$ with discrete simplicial mapping sets: the constant simplicial set on $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal M}(X,Y)$, with its given composition. Here simplicial sets mean [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-set]. Write $\Delta^n_m=\operatorname{Hom}_{\Delta}([m],[n])$. For a simplicial set $K$, let $c(K)$ be its vertices modulo the equivalence relation generated by the two endpoints of each edge. Put $K\otimes X=\coprod_{c(K)}X$ and $Y^K=\prod_{c(K)}Y$, using [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] and its opposite. These are tensors and cotensors for the discrete enrichment. Indeed a simplicial map $K\to D(S)$, with $D(S)$ constant on a set $S$, is exactly a function $c(K)\to S$: every simplex must have the common value of its vertices, and these assignments commute with all operators. Likewise every map $K\times\Delta^n\to D(S)$ is independent of the $\Delta^n$ direction: edges $(s_0v,e)$ join $(v,i)$ to $(v,j)$, and the edges of $K$ at a fixed vertex of $\Delta^n$ impose exactly the original equivalence relation. Thus its internal mapping set is constant on $\operatorname{Hom}(c(K),S)$. The coproduct and product universal properties give the required enriched tensor and cotensor adjunctions, naturally in all variables. This constructs auxiliary enrichment from the given limits and colimits; it imposes no compatibility axiom on the model structure.

source.place: A.2.8.3 reduced to the simplicial enrichment version A.3.3.3 by discrete enrichment; elementary construction supplied here; Stacks 002F (categories.tex, definition-colimit), its dual 002E (definition-limit), and 0175 (simplicial.tex, definition-terminology-simplicial-sets).

proof.text: Regard $A$ as the simplicial category with discrete mapping sets $D(\operatorname{Hom}_A(a,b))$. Enriched functors from this category to the enrichment of step 1 are exactly ordinary functors $A\to\mathcal M$: a map between discrete mapping sets is a function on their vertices, and the enriched identity and composition equations are precisely the ordinary functor equations. The enriched natural-transformation equations are likewise ordinary naturality. Apply [lem-coef-enriched-diagram-size-generation] to these data. It gives that $\mathcal D=\operatorname{Fun}(A,\mathcal M)$ is locally presentable and that all small limits and colimits are computed objectwise. The input local presentability is assumed in the item, and step 1 supplies all the enrichment, tensor and cotensor hypotheses; this cited result requires no simplicial model axiom. Write $W_A,C_A,T_A$ for objectwise weak equivalences, cofibrations and trivial cofibrations. In particular $T_A=C_A\cap W_A$.

source.place: A.2.8.2 and A.3.3.3, ordinary functor categories via discrete enrichment.

proof.text: Choose ground generating sets $I,J$, so that $I^\square=\mathrm{Fib}\cap W$ and $J^\square=\mathrm{Fib}$, where the superscript denotes right diagonal lifting. The ground left classes $\mathrm{Cof}$ and $\mathrm{Cof}\cap W$ are weakly saturated: an isomorphism $i$ lifts against every $p$ by the diagonal $u i^{-1}$ in a square $pu=vi$; [lem-coef-lifting-class-closure] gives pushouts, composites and arrow retracts, and [lem-coef-transfinite-left-lifting] gives small transfinite compositions. Coproducts also preserve either left class, since a lifting square on a coproduct is a small family of squares and the chosen diagonals assemble by the coproduct universal property. The weakly saturated closure of $I$ is exactly $\mathrm{Cof}$. For the nontrivial inclusion, factor a cofibration $f:X\to Y$ as $p i$ by [lem-coef-accessible-small-object-factorization], with $i$ in that closure and $p\in I^\square$. Lifting $f$ against $p$ gives $h:Y\to\operatorname{cod}(i)$ with $hf=i$ and $ph=1_Y$. Thus $(1_X,h)$ and $(1_X,p)$ exhibit $f$ as an arrow retract of $i$. The reverse inclusion holds because $I\subseteq{}^\square(I^\square)=\mathrm{Cof}$ and this class is weakly saturated. For $J$, its weak saturation lies in $\mathrm{Cof}\cap W={}^{\square}(J^\square)$ by this closure argument. Conversely factor any $f\in\mathrm{Cof}\cap W$ as $pi$ with $i$ in the saturation of $J$ and $p\in J^\square=\mathrm{Fib}$. Lifting $f$ against $p$ gives $hf=i$, $ph=1$, so $(1,h),(1,p)$ exhibit $f$ as a retract of $i$. Thus the saturation of $J$ is exactly $\mathrm{Cof}\cap W$.

source.place: A.1.2.5 and the retract argument of A.1.2.7; the two generating sets in the proof of A.2.8.2.

proof.text: Apply the small-generation clause of [lem-coef-enriched-diagram-size-generation] twice, to the discrete enrichment of steps 1-2 and the sets $I,J$ of step 3. There are small sets $S,T$ of arrows of $\mathcal D$ whose weakly saturated closures are respectively $C_A,T_A$. This is precisely generation of the objectwise classes, not just the smaller classes generated by free diagrams. For either $U=S$ or $U=T$, lifting against its closure is equivalent to lifting against $U$: the left lifting class of $U^\square$ contains $U$ and is weakly saturated by [lem-coef-lifting-class-closure] and [lem-coef-transfinite-left-lifting]. Apply [lem-coef-accessible-small-object-factorization] in the locally presentable category $\mathcal D$ to obtain functorial factorizations with left part in $C_A$ and right part in $R_C=C_A^\square$, and similarly with left part in $T_A$ and right part in $R_T=T_A^\square$. These pairs are WFS. For example any map with the left lifting property against $R_C$ is an arrow retract of its $S$-factorization's left part, by the lift and retract equations in step 3. Since $C_A$ is retract closed, that map is in $C_A$; the converse lifting inclusion and the corresponding assertion for $T_A$ hold by their constructions. Both WFS are generated by sets and have the displayed functorial factorizations.

source.place: A.2.8.3 / A.3.3.3, followed by A.1.2.5 and the WFS retract argument; applied to both ground generating sets.

proof.text: For $a\in A$, the evaluation adjunction in [lem-coef-enriched-diagram-size-generation] takes the explicit ordinary form $a_!X(b)=\coprod_{u:a\to b}X$, with transition maps given by postcomposition of the labels $u$. Its adjunction bijection sends $a_!X\to H$ to the component $X\to H(a)$ at $1_a$; the inverse sends the $u$-summand to $H(u)$ after that map. This also identifies commutative squares and diagonals for $a_!i$ against $p$ with those for $i$ against $p_a$. By the coproduct lifting argument of step 3, $a_!i\in C_A$ for every $i\in I$, and $a_!j\in T_A$ for every $j\in J$. Hence $p\in R_C$ implies $p_a\in I^\square=\mathrm{Fib}\cap W$ for every $a$; in particular $R_C\subseteq W_A$. Likewise $p\in R_T$ implies $p_a\in J^\square=\mathrm{Fib}$. This proves the required objectwise fibration assertion once $R_T$ is identified with the injective fibrations.

source.place: Free diagrams in the proof of A.2.8.2; Remark A.2.8.5; the evaluation left-adjoint formula is also part of the cited diagram-generation node.

proof.text: We claim $R_C=R_T\cap W_A$. Since $T_A\subseteq C_A$, one has $R_C\subseteq R_T$, and step 5 gives $R_C\subseteq W_A$. Conversely let $p:X\to Y$ lie in $R_T\cap W_A$, and factor it by the first WFS of step 4 as $p=q i$ with $i\in C_A$ and $q\in R_C$. Since $q,p\in W_A$, objectwise two-out-of-three gives $i\in W_A$, so $i\in T_A$. Lift $i$ against $p$ in the square whose top map is $1_X$ and bottom map is $q$. The diagonal $h$ satisfies $hi=1_X$ and $ph=q$. Thus the arrow maps $(i,1_Y):p\to q$ and $(h,1_Y):q\to p$ exhibit $p$ as a retract of $q$. By the right-class retract closure in [lem-coef-lifting-class-closure], $p\in R_C$. Now $W_A$ is retract closed and satisfies two-out-of-three, because both claims hold at every component in $\mathcal M$. Together with step 4 this gives the model WFS $(C_A,R_T\cap W_A)$ and $(C_A\cap W_A,R_T)$. The model conventions of the item are therefore satisfied, and $R_T$ has exactly the stated injective lifting definition. Step 2 gives local presentability; step 4 gives small generators and functoriality. Thus the model structure is combinatorial.

source.place: A.2.8.2, injective case: explicit two-WFS compatibility verification replacing the general recognition theorem.

proof.text: The universal property of limits, which is the opposite of [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit], gives a natural bijection $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal D}(\Delta X,H)=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal M}(X,\lim_A H)$. A transformation $\Delta i$ has every component $i$, so $\Delta$ preserves cofibrations and trivial cofibrations by step 6. Thus $\Delta\dashv\lim_A$ is a Quillen adjunction. Explicitly, transposing a lifting square for a ground trivial cofibration $i$ against $\lim_A p$ gives a lifting square for $\Delta i\in T_A$ against $p\in R_T$, so $\lim_Ap$ is a fibration. With $i$ a ground cofibration and $p\in R_C$, the same argument makes $\lim_Ap$ a trivial fibration. Thus the strict limit preserves fibrations, trivial fibrations and fibrant objects. For the last assertion, the limit of the terminal diagram is terminal by the same universal property.

source.place: A.2.8.7(2) with A mapping to the terminal category; Stacks 002F (categories.tex, definition-colimit) in the opposite category, tag 002E (definition-limit).

proof.text: For later comparison, the limit also preserves weak equivalences between injectively fibrant diagrams. Indeed for such a weak equivalence $f:X\to Y$, use the fibrant half of [lem-coef-brown-split-factorizations] in the model category of step 6: $f=p i$, where $i$ is a trivial cofibration, $p$ is a fibration and there is a fibration $r$ with $ri=1_X$. Two-out-of-three makes both $p$ and $r$ weak equivalences. Step 7 sends both to trivial fibrations. The identity $(\lim_A r)(\lim_A i)=1$ and two-out-of-three show that $\lim_Ai$ is a weak equivalence, and therefore so is $\lim_Af=(\lim_Ap)(\lim_Ai)$. No simplicial model axiom or properness is used.

source.place: Brown split-factorization argument (pinned Mathlib AlgebraicTopology/ModelCategory/BrownLemma.lean, FibrantBrownFactorization); applied to the right Quillen functor of A.2.8.7(2).

proof.text: Factor $H\to *$ functorially by the second WFS of step 4 as a trivial cofibration $j:H\to RH$ followed by an injective fibration $RH\to *$. For two such replacements $j:H\to F$ and $k:H\to G$, lifting $j$ against $G\to *$ gives $g:F\to G$ with $gj=k$. Two-out-of-three makes $g$ a weak equivalence between fibrant diagrams, so step 8 makes $\lim_Ag$ a weak equivalence, commuting with the comparison maps from $\lim_AH$. Consequently, for every fixed cone with vertex $C$, its comparisons to $\lim_AF$ and $\lim_AG$ are either both weak equivalences or neither is. This also covers any replacement given merely as a weak equivalence $w:H\to F$ with $F$ fibrant: factor $w=qj$ with $j\in C_A$ and $q\in R_C$. Since $w,q$ are weak equivalences, $j$ is a trivial cofibration. Its target $Z$ is fibrant: $q$ is a fibration and so is $F\to *$; right lifting classes are closed under composition by applying [lem-coef-lifting-class-closure] to the opposite category. The limit sends $q$ to a trivial fibration by step 7. Hence the comparisons through $Z\to F$ have the same weak-equivalence test, reducing to the preceding trivial-cofibration replacements.

source.place: A.2.8.7 and definition of homotopy right Kan extension immediately following it: replacement comparison expanded by lifting and two-out-of-three.

proof.text: The homotopy limit here is the right derived strict limit, that is, strict limit after injectively fibrant replacement as in step 9. A cone $C\to\lim_AH$ has comparison to this model given by the composite $C\to\lim_AH\to\lim_ARH$, induced on each projection by $H\to RH$. By the model-category definition of a homotopy-limit cone, it is homotopy limiting exactly when this comparison is a weak equivalence. Step 9 shows explicitly that this condition is independent of all replacements, even those not chosen as trivial cofibrations. Step 8 supplies the homotopical invariance needed for this right-derived computation. If $A=\varnothing$, the diagram category has one object and one morphism, both WFS are the unique ones, and its strict limit in $\mathcal M$ is terminal. All component conditions above are vacuous, and the final criterion reads exactly that $C\to *$ is a weak equivalence. No nonemptiness, cofibrancy of values or simplicial enrichment of the input model category has entered.

lean.statement: theorem combinatorial_injective_diagram_model {A : Type w} [SmallCategory A] {M : Type u} [Category.{v} M] [ModelCategory M] [HasLimits M] [HasColimits M] [HasLimitsOfSize.{w, w} M] [HasColimitsOfSize.{w, w} M] (hM : CombinatorialModelCategory.{u, v, max v w} M) : ∃ S : ModelCategory (A ⥤ M), @CombinatorialModelCategory.{max u v w, max v w, max v w} (A ⥤ M) inferInstance S ∧ S.categoryWithWeakEquivalences.weakEquivalences = (weakEquivalences M).functorCategory A ∧ S.categoryWithCofibrations.cofibrations = (cofibrations M).functorCategory A ∧ S.categoryWithFibrations.fibrations = ((trivialCofibrations M).functorCategory A).rlp ∧ S.categoryWithFibrations.fibrations ≤ (fibrations M).functorCategory A ∧ Nonempty ((Functor.const A : M ⥤ (A ⥤ M)) ⊣ lim) ∧ (∀ (X Y : M) (f : X ⟶ Y), cofibrations M f → S.categoryWithCofibrations.cofibrations ((Functor.const A).map f)) ∧ (∀ (X Y : M) (f : X ⟶ Y), trivialCofibrations M f → (S.categoryWithCofibrations.cofibrations ⊓ S.categoryWithWeakEquivalences.weakEquivalences) ((Functor.const A).map f)) ∧ (∀ (H R : A ⥤ M) (j : H ⟶ R) (c : Cone H), (weakEquivalences M).functorCategory A j → S.categoryWithFibrations.fibrations (terminal.from R) → (IsInjectiveHomotopyLimit c ↔ weakEquivalences M (limit.lift H c ≫ lim.map j)))
